extracted.intended_audience: GAP users and package developers (mathematicians / computational group theorists)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference guidance for GAP character-theory tests (primitivity, monomiality, etc.) and for installing, loading, and developing GAP packages (package paths, autoloading, kernel extensions, logging).

rubrics_metrics.name: TestHomogeneous result components
rubrics_metrics.description: TestHomogeneous returns a record describing whether a character's restriction to a normal subgroup is homogeneous. The record contains at least isHomogeneous (true/false) and comment (string), and may include character (an irreducible constituent) and multiplicity (multiplicity in the restriction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how to inspect test.isHomogeneous, test.comment, test.character, test.multiplicity and test.character's Degree. Use the class positions of a normal subgroup when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPrimitiveCharacter (primitivity criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPrimitiveCharacter(chi) returns true iff the character chi is not induced from any proper subgroup (currently implemented only for characters of solvable groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to test primitivity of irreducible characters; examples show true/false for Irr(SL(2,3)) entries. See also TestQuasiPrimitive for related checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiprimitivity (TestQuasiPrimitive / IsQuasiPrimitive)
rubrics_metrics.description: A character chi is quasiprimitive iff it restricts homogeneously to every normal subgroup of its group. TestQuasiPrimitive returns a record with isQuasiPrimitive (true/false), comment, and, if not quasiprimitive, a character component (an irreducible constituent of a nonhomogeneous restriction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: for solvable groups, quasiprimitivity equals primitivity. Examples demonstrate rec( comment := "all restrictions checked", isQuasiPrimitive := true ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced-from-normal-subgroup test
rubrics_metrics.description: TestInducedFromNormalSubgroup(chi[, N]) / IsInducedFromNormalSubgroup(chi) determine whether an irreducible character chi is induced from a proper normal subgroup of G; if N is given it checks induction from that N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result record always contains isInduced (true/false) and comment. If true, character contains a character of a maximal normal subgroup from which chi is induced. Examples include List(Irr(SL(2,3)), IsInducedFromNormalSubgroup).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomial character and monomial group definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A character χ of G is monomial if χ is induced from a linear character of some subgroup. A group G is monomial (M-group) if every ordinary irreducible character of G is monomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions underpin the TestMonomial family of operations and related classification tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestMonomial (monomiality testing behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: TestMonomial called with a character or group returns a record describing monomiality: isMonomial (true/false/"?") and comment, and possibly character (a linear character from which chi is induced, or a nonmonomial character if group declared nonmonomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional boolean uselattice argument controls whether the subgroup lattice may be computed. If lattice is disallowed and no proof is possible, isMonomial may be "?". Examples: TestMonomial(S4) gives rec( comment := "abelian by supersolvable group", isMonomial := true ).

rubrics_metrics.name: TestMonomialUseLattice (when to use subgroup lattice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Global variable TestMonomialUseLattice controls for which group orders TestMonomial may compute the subgroup lattice; can be a positive integer or infinity; default 1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting this affects whether TestMonomial will attempt potentially expensive lattice computations and thus whether it can reach a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMonomialNumber (numerical criterion for monomiality of all solvable groups of order n)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsMonomialNumber(n) returns true iff every solvable group of order n is monomial. There exists a solvable nonmonomial group of order n iff one of five explicit arithmetic conditions on the prime-power factorization of n holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five possibilities (paraphrased): (1) ν2(n)≥2 and some p has νp(n)≥3 and p≡−1 mod 4; (2) ν2(n)≥3 and some p has νp(n)≥3 and p≡1 mod 4; (3) odd primes p,q dividing n with ord(p,q) even and ord(p,q) < νp(n) (esp. νp(n)≥3); (4) exists q with ν2(n) ≥ 2 ord(2,q) + 2 (esp. ν2(n)≥4); (5) ν2(n)≥2 and some p with p≡1 mod 4, ord(p,q) odd, and 2 ord(p,q) < νp(n) (esp. νp(n)≥3). These correspond to the five types of solvable minimal nonmonomial groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestMonomialQuick (cheap monomiality heuristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: TestMonomialQuick performs inexpensive checks (no character table computations) returning isMonomial (true/false/"?") and comment explaining the reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups proved monomial: nilpotent, Sylow abelian by supersolvable, or solvable with no prime dividing the order to the third power. Nonsolvable groups are proved nonmonomial. Characters proved monomial if linear, codegree is a prime power, group's known monomial, or factor modulo kernel provable monomial. Examples show rec( comment := "whole group is monomial", isMonomial := true ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subnormally monomial (SM) definition and test
rubrics_metrics.description: An irreducible character is subnormally monomial (SM) if it is induced from a linear character of a subnormal subgroup; a group is SM if all irreducible characters are SM. TestSubnormallyMonomial and IsSubnormallyMonomial report isSubnormallyMonomial (true/false) and comment, and may include a non-SM character if false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate detection of non-SM characters and reporting of reasons (e.g., "found non-SM character").

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative SM (TestRelativelySM / IsRelativelySM)
rubrics_metrics.description: TestRelativelySM(G or chi[, N]) tests whether a SM group G or its irreducible character chi is relatively SM w.r.t. every normal subgroup (or w.r.t. a specific normal subgroup N): existence of a subnormal subgroup H ≥ N such that characters are induced from ψ of H with ψ|_N irreducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result record contains isRelativelySM (true/false) and comment; if not relatively SM for some normal subgroup, a character component gives a witness. Note it does not check whether G is SM initially.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMinimalNonmonomial (minimal nonmonomial group definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsMinimalNonmonomial(G) returns true iff G is nonmonomial and all proper subgroups and factor groups of G are monomial (i.e., G is minimal nonmonomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to test minimal obstructions; examples include IsMinimalNonmonomial(SL(2,3)) returning true.

rubrics_metrics.name: MinimalNonmonomialGroup construction parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: MinimalNonmonomialGroup(p, factsize) constructs (if exists) a solvable minimal nonmonomial group determined by prime p and factsize, where factsize (size of the Fitting factor's factor) must be one of {4,8,odd prime, twice an odd prime, four times an odd prime}; in some cases centre order is 2p+1 and p divides F(K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification reference: van der Waall. Examples show specific returned group structures for particular (p,factsize) inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestSubnormallyMonomial / TestRelativelySM result conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: All these Test* functions return records with a boolean-like field (named isXxx or similar) and a comment string explaining the reason; when they disprove a property they often provide a witness character in 'character'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general pattern across character-testing operations and should be expected when scripting checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package installation layout requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A GAP package is a collection of files in a single directory which must be a subdirectory of the pkg directory in one of GAP's root directories (or placed in a private root directory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Downloaded/cloned package archives include README files that explain installation steps. Some packages require compilation (./configure; make) or running BuildPackages.sh in pkg. Windows users may not be able to use some external binaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: LoadPackage usage and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: LoadPackage(name[, version][, banner]) loads the named package (case-insensitive, abbreviation allowed). If version is given, only load that version or newer (or exact when prefixed with '='). Optional banner controls printing. Returns true if loaded or already loaded, fail if cannot be loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If abbreviation ambiguous, LoadPackage returns fail listing completions. Use TestPackageAvailability and DisplayPackageLoadingLog to diagnose failures. LoadPackage returns true without action if the package is already loaded in a sufficient version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic package loading and disabling
rubrics_metrics.description: Some packages are loaded automatically at GAP startup: 'needed' packages required to start GAP, and 'default' packages. Autoloading can be suppressed with -A, by putting package names in the user preference 'ExcludeFromAutoload', or by adding a NOAUTO file in a pkg directory. Missing needed packages cause an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAPInfo.Dependencies.NeededOtherPackages lists required packages. Autoloading suppression still signals missing 'needed' packages. Use SetPackagePath, ExtendRootDirectories, or ExtendPackageDirectories to affect which versions/locations are visible during a session (but not startup).

rubrics_metrics.name: SetPackagePath (force package version selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: SetPackagePath(pkgname, pkgpath) forces GAP to load the version of pkgname found at pkgpath by erasing other available-version info and storing the PackageInfo.g record at pkgpath. If pkgname is already loaded from a different path, SetPackagePath signals an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call SetPackagePath immediately before LoadPackage. ExtendPackageDirectories/ExtendRootDirectories may change available versions later.

rubrics_metrics.name: ExtendRootDirectories / ExtendPackageDirectories behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: ExtendRootDirectories(paths) and ExtendPackageDirectories(paths) add directories to GAPInfo.RootPaths or GAPInfo.PackageDirectories respectively and reinitialize available packages so LoadPackage can find packages in those directories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ExtendRootDirectories does not affect GAP startup (GAP library loaded earlier). These functions are for making packages available after GAP has started.

rubrics_metrics.name: DisplayPackageLoadingLog and severity levels
rubrics_metrics.description: DisplayPackageLoadingLog([severity]) shows package-loading log messages whose severity is at most severity; severity levels in increasing order: PACKAGE_ERROR, PACKAGE_WARNING, PACKAGE_INFO, PACKAGE_DEBUG. Log messages are collected during package consideration/loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended meanings: PACKAGE_ERROR for errors that will stop package loading, PACKAGE_WARNING for missing but solvable issues (e.g., missing binary), PACKAGE_INFO for incompatibility or unclear issues, PACKAGE_DEBUG for detailed loading steps. Use SetUserPreference("InfoPackageLoadingLevel", level) to see messages as they arise; LogPackageLoadingMessage allows packages to add messages (severity and optional package name).

rubrics_metrics.name: ReadPackage / RereadPackage semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ReadPackage([name,] file) reads file from a package's home directory into the package namespace; RereadPackage is similar but also overwrites read-only globals. If file readable, ReadPackage returns true, otherwise Warns (ReadPackage) or returns false (RereadPackage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-argument form is allowed but not recommended because it assumes package name equals first part of file path. Absolute path resolution differs depending on whether package is loaded or merely available.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestPackageAvailability semantics and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: TestPackageAvailability(name[, version][, checkall]) tests whether a package is available: returns true if already loaded, fail if not available, or a string path where the package resides if available but not loaded. If checkall true, all dependencies are checked even if earlier failures occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TestPackageAvailability before DisplayPackageLoadingLog(PACKAGE_INFO) to get reasons why a package cannot be loaded. Do not call TestPackageAvailability inside a package's AvailabilityTest because it calls that test function.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPackageLoaded and IsPackageMarkedForLoading
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPackageLoaded(name[, version]) returns true if the package is already loaded in at least the requested version, false otherwise. IsPackageMarkedForLoading(name, version) indicates whether the package will be loaded after the current LoadPackage call sequence (i.e., already requested as needed/suggested).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Version comparisons obey CompareVersionNumbers semantics; names are case-insensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestPackage (run package-defined standard test)
rubrics_metrics.description: TestPackage(pkgname) checks that the package is loadable and has a standard test defined in its PackageInfo.g, then runs that test in the current session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test behavior depends on the package and current session state (loaded packages, globals, RNG, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: InstalledPackageVersion (version inquiry)
rubrics_metrics.description: InstalledPackageVersion(name) returns the version string of the loaded package, or the version string of the version that would be loaded if the package is available but not yet loaded; returns fail if not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that loading other packages might change which version would be loaded and thus change the result after additional loads. Argument name is case-insensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: DirectoriesPackageLibrary and DirectoriesPackagePrograms
rubrics_metrics.description: DirectoriesPackageLibrary(name[, path]) returns the library directory path(es) for a package's library files (default path "lib"), while DirectoriesPackagePrograms(name) returns the directory for external binaries (bin/architecture) for the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second argument is required to find deeper-than-one-level subdirectories. Path separators should be '/' even on Windows. Examples show expected dir(...) outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CompareVersionNumbers behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: CompareVersionNumbers(supplied, required[, "equal"]) splits version strings at non-digit chars into integer lists and compares lexicographically to test whether supplied ≥ required (or equal if "equal" specified). A version ending in 'dev' is considered infinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts flexible version strings like "3.141.59", "5 release 2 patchlevel 666". Use this for reliable version checks in package loading.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeclareAutoreadableVariables
rubrics_metrics.description: DeclareAutoreadableVariables(pkgname, filename, varlist) notifies GAP that the variables named in varlist are bound when the given file is read; on first access to one of the variables, the file will be read automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for lazy loading of package data: specify package name and file relative to package home directory and list of global variable names (strings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel modules in packages and kernel-extension API
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages may include kernel modules (C code) which can be compiled using the gac script to produce dynamically loadable modules; such modules should be loaded using LoadKernelExtension(pkgname[, modname]); IsKernelExtensionAvailable(pkgname[, modname]) checks availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend naming kernel extension to match package name if only one extension; PackageInfo.g should define an AvailabilityTest calling IsKernelExtensionAvailable if kernel module required. LoadKernelExtension provides better error messages than the older LoadDynamicModule approach. Examples: gap4/gac -d test.c produces test.so, load with LoadKernelExtension("SomePackage").

rubrics_metrics.name: LoadDynamicModule (legacy dynamic module loading)
rubrics_metrics.description: LoadDynamicModule(filename) loads a compiled dynamic module file into GAP (legacy API still available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On some OSes, reloading a file with the same filename may have no effect even if the file changed on disk.
